html:
The Basilika, "the imperial laws", is a great collection of Byzantine law in 60 books, completed around 892 under Emperor Leo VI the Wise. It finished work begun by his father Basil I to bring the law of Justinian I up to date.

Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis was mostly in Latin, which few in the Greek-speaking empire could read, and full of rules that no longer applied. The Basilika put it into Greek and arranged it by subject, bringing the matching parts of the Code, the Digest, the Institutes and the later Novels together in one place. Laws that were out of date were dropped.

It became the main body of law for the rest of the Byzantine Empire, and notes called scholia were added to it over the next centuries. Shorter handbooks such as the Hexabiblos drew on it, and through them it shaped law in Greece until the 20th century. Scholars of Roman law still use it to fill gaps in the texts of Justinian.
sum: The Basilika, "the imperial laws", is a great collection of Byzantine law in 60 books, completed around 892 under Emperor Leo VI the Wise. It finished work begun by his father Basil I to bring the law of Justinian I up to date.
